item.title: Infantino inspects Warri Stadium, pledges FIFA support during visit
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye FIFA President Gianni Infantino has inspected the remodeled Warri City Stadium and pledged the world football body’s continued support for Nigerian football. Infantino visited the Delta State facility on Friday with FIFA Secretary-General Mattias Grafström, ahead of its scheduled commissioning on Saturday. He was received at Osubi Airport by Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and former Nigeria Football Federation president Amaju Pinnick. Infantino praised the Delta State Government’s investment, saying modern sports facilities could help develop young talent and expand opportunities for boys and girls. He also celebrated Nigeria’s football heritage, highlighting the country’s contribution to the global game. “This stadium is fantastic. It has everything you can dream of. I just would love to wear some shorts and kick the ball,” he said, adding that he hoped to return and play there once the remaining work was completed. The FIFA president also congratulated Nigeria’s U-17 women’s team, the Flamingos, on winning the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, describing their triumph as a source of pride. “You will always count on FIFA and on the FIFA president as your not just partner, but your family member,” Infantino said. Oborevwori said the inspection was an opportunity to assess the stadium’s readiness against international standards. In a post on X, the governor described the renovation as extensive and said the state remained committed to delivering world-class sports infrastructure. He wrote: “It was a pleasure to welcome the President of FIFA, Gianni Infantino, to Osubi this morning. We thereafter proceeded to the Warri Stadium, where we inspected the facility to assess its readiness against international standards,” “The transformation is extensive, and our commitment remains to deliver world-class sporting infrastructure that will position Delta State to compete on the global stage and emerge as a hub for sporting excellence. In the words of the FIFA President, Gianni Infantino: “This is fantastic!” It was a pleasure to welcome the President of FIFA, Gianni Infantino, to Osubi this morning. We thereafter proceeded to the Warri Stadium, where we inspected the facility to assess its readiness against international standards. During his visit, he also stressed the importance of bringing football closer to communities through local facilities. Infantino’s visit to Warri is among several trips he has made to Nigeria since becoming FIFA president. item.title: Naira depreciates to N1,472/$ in parallel market
item.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan The Naira today appreciated to N1,472 per dollar from N1,468 per dollar in the parallel market on Thursday. Similarly, the naira depreciated to N1,394 per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, NFEM. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, showed that the indicative exchange rate for the official market rose to N1,394 per dollar from N1388 per dollar on Thursday, indicating N6 depreciation for the naira. Consequently, the margin between the parallel and official markets narrowed to N78 per dollar from N80 per dollar on Thursday. The value of interbank turnover in NFEM rose by 1.9 percent to $815.6 billion from $800.3 billion on Thursday. item.title: Denmark expels Russian diplomat over attempt to kill Ukrainian rapper
item.description: Denmark’s foreign minister on Friday said Moscow’s defence attache in Copenhagen would be expelled after Russia was suspected of being behind an attempted assassination of a Ukrainian rapper. “We have just summoned the Russian ambassador to the ministry of foreign affairs and notified him of the government’s decision to expel the Russian defence attache from Denmark” within seven days, Lars Lokke Rasmussen told a news conference. “We are saying this very clearly: we have exposed you”, he said. He also added Denmark was mulling suspending Schengen visas to Russians. “We have launched work at the European level to further tighten the rules governing access of Russian nationals to Europe,” he said. “We are now stepping up our efforts — towards a halt to all non-essential visas”. “The strongest response Denmark can give is not to waver and to support Ukraine. And we fully intend to continue” supporting Ukraine, he said. The announcements came after Danish intelligence said it suspected Russia of planning the assassination of a Ukrainian rapper during a concert in a Copenhagen suburb with the help of a Danish criminal gang. Denmark’s public television DR identified the rapper as Kyivstoner, who holds both Ukrainian and American citizenship. cbw/nzg/eab/phz Vanguard News The post Denmark expels Russian diplomat over attempt to kill Ukrainian rapper appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027 Election: ‘What President Tinubu is thinking about’
item.description: …targets 18/18 victory for APC in Cross River By Ike Uchechukwu – CALABAR Minister of State for Industry, Sen. John Owan-Enoh, says President Bola Tinubu is focused on building a prosperous future for Nigerians rather than winning the next election. Owan-Enoh stated this on Friday at Ikom Township Stadium during the inauguration of the Cross River chapter of Project Beyond’s executive and polling unit structures for the Central and Northern Senatorial Districts of the state. He described Tinubu as a pragmatic leader whose decisions were driven by long-term national development rather than immediate political considerations. The minister likened Tinubu’s leadership approach to that of Singapore’s founding Prime Minister, Lee Kuan Yew, whom he credited with transforming the Asian country into a global success story. “That Prime Minister didn’t look at politics the same way a politician looks at the next election. That Prime Minister looked at the next generation. “That is what President Bola Tinubu is doing,” he said. Owan-Enoh acknowledged that the President’s economic reforms had subjected many Nigerians to hardship but described the situation as temporary sacrifices necessary for economic recovery. He likened the reforms to bitter medicine that would eventually restore the country’s economic health. “That tablet is bitter. But after that bitterness, you’ll get well,” he said. According to him, Nigeria has begun experiencing economic recovery and stability after three and a half years of the administration’s policies. He said the administration’s next priority was to translate the gains into prosperity and improved purchasing power for Nigerians. “Three and a half years later, recovery has started. Stability has set in, and I think for President Tinubu, the next concentration is prosperity. “The next concentration is the power of your pocket,” he said. The minister further said inflation had declined to about 14 per cent and expressed optimism that it would continue falling towards single digits. He urged Cross River residents to support Tinubu’s re-election, saying the state needed to remain influential in national decision-making. “You will need to sit at the table when decisions are taken for you to be able to put before that table what you want,” he said. Owan-Enoh said securing the state’s political relevance required a strong electoral showing for the APC in 2027. He recalled that Tinubu won seven of Cross River’s 18 local government areas in the 2023 presidential election. He, however, challenged party members to work towards securing victory in all 18 local government areas in the Jan. 16, 2027 election. “In 2023, out of 18 local governments, the President won seven. “In 2027, we must leave here with a determination and a resolve that, come Jan. 16, 2027, Mr President is going to win 18 over 18 in Cross River, and that is possible,” he said Vanguard News The post 2027 Election: ‘What President Tinubu is thinking about’ appeared first on V

item.title: Poland and allies say Russian missile a ‘provocation’ from Moscow
item.description: Warsaw and its allies said Friday that a Russian missile landing in Poland was a “provocation” from Moscow as thousands of European troops were holding exercises nearby. Poland said two Russian missiles hit its territory early on Friday, landing in southeastern Poland as drills were due to take place. Nobody was hurt, Poland said. Authorities said one Kh-101 missile was confirmed to have landed in the eastern village of Nowy Lipowiec. A second missile is suspected to have hit another location and a jet-powered drone a third. The projectiles crossed into the NATO country as Russia pounded neighbouring Ukraine and thousands of European troops were holding unprecedented army drills in southeastern Poland. Several European defence ministers were in Poland for the drills. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said everything pointed to the fact that these were not accidental stray missiles. “Three Russian objects violated Polish airspace. They fell on Polish land. One exploded. There is no destruction, no casualties,” he said, adding: “This is not just my opinion but of our foreign partners and NATO: this does not look like a coincidence.” He said he believed the incident was linked to the European drills. “We are dealing with an intentional provocation,” he added. He said the objects “fell close” to where “armies of the Coalition of the Willing” were training in Nowa Deba, southeastern Poland. “Coalition of the Willing” refers to a group of Ukraine’s European backers who are prepared to send peacekeeping troops to the country. Nowy Lipowiec, where the first missile fell, is a 1.5-hour drive from where the drills are taking place. Just a day before the incident, US media outlet Fox News quoted Donald Trump as saying Russian leader Vladimir Putin “has been landing drones in Poland, and a couple of little missiles, by mistake”. Tusk said on Friday that Poland would give the United States access to the missile debris. “I don’t always agree with the interpretation of the US side on these incidents. We are cooperating with the Americans. They have access to the places, to the debris of the objects.” The Kremlin has not yet commented. The missiles flew in as Russian strikes killed at least eight people in Ukraine, a day after Putin met with Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping. ‘Putin seeks confrontation’ UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the “incursion into Polish airspace is utterly unacceptable”, while the EU said it stood in “full solidarity” with the Poles. Germany said the incident was “yet another example of Russia’s ongoing provocations” and that “rather than showing a willingness to negotiate, Putin… continues to seek confrontation”. The French presidency called it a “serious incident”. item.title: Akpabio charges APC support groups against electoral violence
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA- THE President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio has urged support groups and members of the All Progressives Congress, APC, not to allow themselves to be provoked to carry out attacks or retaliate against members of the opposition as the party was better positioned to win in a free and fair election. Senator Akpabio gave the charge in Abuja on Friday at the inauguration of “Tinubu Again Movement” a grassroots mobilization movement, convened by the Minister of State for Defence, Dr Bello Matawalle, aimed at securing more than 20 million votes for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in 2027. In a statement signed by the Special Assistant on Media/Communication to the President of the Senate, Anietie Ekong, Akpabio urged the APC members and supporters not to be distracted by the antics of the opposition parties who aimed to attract sympathy by inciting violence in the run up to the election. The President of the Senate said: “Please be careful. Don’t allow them to provoke you to violence. Because they know they are losing, they will sponsor some misguided youths to throw stones at you. If they throw stones at you, your target is to garner votes and defeat them. “By January 16, 2027, they will know the difference between stones and votes. When you are certain of winning you don’t deploy stones and violence as your weapons but you persuade them with the monumental achievement of the APC administration.” Akpabio charged the members of Tinubu Again Movement to carry the message of the Renewed Hope administration to their various polling units, wards and local government areas to sensitize the populace on the achievement of the administration of President Tinubu. Akpabio who was the Chairman at the inauguration, reeled out some of the achievements of the administration to include, the Lagos – Calabar coastal highway, the Sokoto – Badagry highway, and other road infrastructure across the States. He said the economy of the country had almost collapsed before the advent of rhe Tinubu administration and commended the administration for the courageous removal of fuel subsidy which he said had made more funds available to States and Local Governments to execute projects without resorting to borrowing. According to him, the introduction of the Students Loan Fund had made it possible for indigent students to access education just as the tax reforms had recaliberated the economy, adding, “Today the States are benefitting from the economic reforms. Many Governors are executing projects without borrowing a dime because of the ingenuity of one man, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. “So when you go out there to talk about how President Tinubu must be returned to office with over 20 million votes, say it with boldness because this President had stabilized and grown the economy and the indices are there for all to see!” Akpabio commended Dr Matawalle for the initiative in convening the Tinubu Again Movement and urged other political appointees to em

item.title: Russia pummels Ukraine, missile hits Poland, after Putin threat
item.description: Moscow pounded Ukraine with massive strikes Friday, with Kyiv saying at least seven people were killed in the capital, while neighbouring Poland accused Moscow of “provocation” after two Russian missiles likely landed in the southeast corner of the NATO country. Russia’s Vladimir Putin had vowed a “painful” response to Kyiv’s strikes on Moscow’s Crimea bridge after holding a summit with China’s Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump. Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky called the night-time strikes one of Moscow’s largest of the nearly five-year war, denouncing what he said was Russian “terror”. Zelensky, who met allies in Berlin Thursday, said Putin’s attempts to “redraw the world” with Xi and Trump had been a “failure”. In China, Putin said he “shared responsibility” for global peace with Xi and Trump and issued a “declaration toward peace” that made no mention of Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine. AFP journalists saw people hunkered down in Kyiv’s metro stations, which double as overnight air-raid shelters, sleeping on yoga mats, camping chairs and in pop-up tents. Kateryna Liubychenko, 32, took her toddler down to try to get some sleep through the bombardment. “It’s painful to have to stop our child from living,” she told AFP. Two people were killed in Lviv, power was knocked out in swathes of the country and in Kyiv, three vital transport bridges were hit, officials said. Explosions rang out through the night as Ukrainian officials reported more than 80 missiles and 400 drones were fired. Three bridges that cross the Dnipro river were hit, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said, threatening yet more disruption to daily life in the city. France requested a UN Security Council meeting over the strikes, saying “Russia will have to answer for its actions there”. Poland decries ‘provocation’ In neighbouring Poland, authorities said one missile was confirmed to have landed in the eastern village of Nowy Lipowiec, with another missile and a jet-powered drone suspected to have hit two other locations. Warsaw said no-one was hurt. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the weapons flying into Poland were deliberate. “The provocation may have been linked with the fact that there are (military) exercises taking place on the territory of Poland,” Tusk told a televised press conference in Warsaw. Thousands of European troops are taking part in military exercises in southeastern Poland. “Nobody can say that this was an innocent coincidence,” Tusk said, adding he had informed NATO “straight away”. Tusk said that NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte would be in Warsaw on Saturday and that he would inform him of the incident. Poland is one of five countries Europe picked to represent it at future US-led talks on Ukraine. Bridge retaliation Russia, which has refused a ceasefire, has increased its strikes as temperatures dip in Ukraine, with many fearing this winter could be the worst of the war yet. item.title: Viral Video: Military uniforms found with bandits not from us – DHQ
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Defence headquarters has denied supplying military camouflage uniforms allegedly found in the possession of suspected bandits in a viral social media video, insisting that the clothing did not originate from the Nigerian military. Read Also: Viral Video: ‘We recovered 12 AK-47 rifles, kidnap victims’ – Military defends engagement with bandits The footage, circulating widely online, showed large quantities of woodland and desert camouflage uniforms spread on the ground, Several others were packed in sacks and allegedly held by suspected bandits. Reacting to the video, the Director of Defence Media Operations, Maj. Gen. Michael Onoja ruled out the possibility that the uniforms were supplied by the military. “That is not possible,” he said, when asked whether the clothing originated from the Nigerian military. Onoja also dismissed suggestions that the uniforms might have been stolen from military supply vehicles attacked by bandits, saying no such incident had been reported. “No such report has been made. It is not from the Nigerian military,” he added. The video reportedly showed two different camouflage patterns, identified as woodland and desert designs, raising renewed concerns over the circulation of military clothing among criminal groups and unauthorised persons. The development comes amid longstanding concerns about criminals, impersonating security personnel to perpetrate attacks, kidnappings and other crimes. In February 2024, the Federal Government reiterated restrictions on the unauthorised use of military camouflage by civilians, warning against the misuse of security uniforms and equipment by criminal elements Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle had stated that the restrictions were necessary to enable security agencies to distinguish legitimate personnel from impostors. He noted that criminals had exploited military and other security agencies’ uniforms to deceive members of the public and facilitate criminal activities. The government’s position was aimed at curbing impersonation, preventing the misuse of military uniforms and strengthening security operations across the country. item.title: Boat capsizes with 300 passengers in Bayelsa
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa A tragedy struck the riverine enclave of Southern Ijaw Local Government Area on Friday, as a cargo boat conveying over 300 passengers capsized, leaving many feared dead. The ill-fated vessel was reportedly en route to Ukubie community from Anyama Ijaw, when the incident occurred at 12 noon. According to preliminary reports, the boat, which was heavily overloaded with passengers traveling for a burial ceremony, went down in the waterways between Oweikorogha and Angiama communities. Eyewitness accounts indicate that the tragedy might have been averted. It was learned that some passengers had suggested the boat stop at Oweikorogha to decongest the vessel, but the advice was allegedly ignored. The boat reportedly capsized shortly after departing the community. While the actual casualty figure remains unconfirmed, fears are mounting that the death toll could be substantial given the number of persons on board. Mr. Ipigansi Igoniba, Chairman of the State Maritime Workers Union, confirmed the incident to our correspondent but stated that information regarding the disaster was still hazy. “I cannot give the casualty figure right now. We have sent our members to the scene of the accident and search and rescue efforts for the missing persons are ongoing,” Igoniba said. Rescue operations are currently underway, though independent confirmation of the number of survivors or fatalities is yet to be established. The incident has cast a pall of mourning over the community, highlighting once again the dangers of overcrowding and unsafe travel on the state’s waterways. item.title: MultiChoice cuts entry-level DStv, GOtv subscriptions to ₦6,000
item.description: MultiChoice Nigeria has introduced restructured DStv and GOtv subscription packages, with entry-level options starting at ₦6,000, following customer feedback on affordability and content preferences. The company’s Chief Executive Officer, Kemi Omotosho, disclosed this during an interview on the Global Business Report on ARISE News on Friday, saying the new packages were designed to simplify subscription choices and provide customers with access to entertainment, sports and other content. She said the company had listened to its subscribers and adjusted its offerings to better address their needs. “We recognised that our customers are dear to us, so we listened to our customers, we simplified our offerings,” she said. Under the new arrangement, DStv subscribers can choose from four packages: Starter, Select, Sports and Premium, while GOtv offers Easy, Starter, Select and Sports. Omotosho said the Starter package, which costs ₦6,000, provides access to more than 90 channels, including Africa Magic Plus, the Premier League Match of the Week, selected UEFA Champions League matches and La Liga coverage. She also explained that the Sports package had been redesigned from the former Compact offering to provide broader access to major sporting competitions. According to her, the package includes all Premier League and Champions League matches, as well as UFC and WWE content, alongside channels available on the Starter and Select packages. Clarifying the subscription rates, Omotosho said the Sports package costs ₦21,000 for new subscribers, while the ₦19,000 rate applies only to existing Compact subscribers migrating to the new package. “When you move into the new pack, it’s ₦21,000 on the Sports pack,” she said. The CEO also highlighted the benefits of MultiChoice Nigeria’s integration into the Canal+ Group, which operates in more than 70 countries across Africa, Asia and Europe. She said the integration had strengthened the company’s capacity in content acquisition, technology and partnerships while retaining its focus on the Nigerian market. “We’re basically riding on global muscle, but we still want to be very relevant to the Nigerian consumer,” she stated. On the company’s transition towards digital entertainment, Omotosho said MultiChoice regarded satellite television and streaming services as complementary platforms rather than competing products. “For us, streaming is not an ‘either/or,’ it is ‘and’,” she said. She cited DStv Stream, which enables subscribers to access television content online without a satellite dish or decoder. According to her, the company’s technology-agnostic approach allows customers to choose satellite television for reliability in areas with limited broadband access or streaming services for greater flexibility. item.title: AI-generated fake content threatens democracy, national security – Okonkwo
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Executive Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Professor Obiora Okonkwo, has expressed concerns over the growing sophistication of artificial intelligence, AI, saying its capacity to generate convincing fake images, videos and voices poses fresh threats to democracy, national security and public trust, particularly during elections. Okonkwo warned that hate speech, misinformation and irresponsible communication could be as destructive as weapons, saying the 1994 Rwandan genocide was an example of how manipulated information could incite mass violence, destroy lives and destabilise nations. He spoke while delivering the opening address at the African session of the World Public Relations Forum, WPRF, Abuja 2026, where he challenged journalists, public relations practitioners, advertisers and corporate communication professionals to strengthen self-regulation and uphold ethical standards to prevent communication platforms from becoming instruments of propaganda and social division. Speaking on the theme, ‘Responsible Communication in Africa: The Importance of Self-Regulation and Information and Media Literacy,’ he said the influence of communication demanded greater responsibility from those who shaped public opinion. He said: “The lesson is unmistakable. Communication is not always an innocent exercise. In the hands of irresponsible actors, the microphone can become as disruptive as a very dangerous weapon.” He said the 2023 general elections were an example of the dangers of irresponsible communication, adding that although social media facilitated political mobilisation, it also enabled the circulation of fabricated election results, unverified claims and divisive ethnic and political narratives. He recalled that the European Union Election Observation Mission documented misleading political communication during the polls, warning that such practices could undermine public confidence in democratic institutions and citizens’ ability to make informed electoral choices. He said: “In an age of unprecedented information flow, the credibility, integrity and social value of what we communicate are as important as the freedom and the platforms through which we communicate.” The airline chairman also cited the COVID-19 pandemic, when the World Health Organisation identified an infodemic of false and misleading information that confused populations, encouraged risky behaviour and weakened confidence in public health institutions. He said misinformation surrounding Ebola outbreaks in parts of the Democratic Republic of Congo similarly fuelled distrust of health workers and undermined disease-control interventions. “These examples demonstrate that irresponsible communication can threaten not only democratic stability but also human lives,” he warned. item.title: ASUU Suspends Taraba Varsity Strike After Gov Kefas’ Intervention
item.description: The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Taraba State University chapter, has conditionally suspended its ongoing strike. The union resolved to suspend the total, comprehensive and indefinite strike, which began on 12 October 2026, with effect from 20 November 2026, following Governor Agbu Kefas’ approval of the full implementation of the 2025 agreement between the Federal Government and ASUU. The decision was reached at a congress held on Friday to determine the union’s position on the governor’s appeal for the suspension of the industrial action and his approval of the agreement’s implementation. This was contained in a statement issued by the ASUU chairman at Taraba State University, Garba Mbave. ASUU-TSU had embarked on the strike over the Taraba State Government’s failure to implement the 2025 Federal Government-ASUU remuneration agreement and pay outstanding salary arrears accrued from January 2026. The union had earlier engaged the state government on the demands, but commenced the indefinite industrial action on October 12 after efforts to resolve the dispute failed. A file photo of Governor of Taraba State Agbu Kefas. Photo: Facebook/Agbu Kefas The union expressed profound appreciation to Kefas, the Commissioner for Tertiary Education, the Head of Service and the university management for their interventions, constructive engagement and commitment towards resolving the industrial dispute. The union also appreciated members of the public, students, parents, staff and the entire university community for their patience, understanding, solidarity and cooperation throughout the strike. “The support, restraint and confidence demonstrated during this challenging period are highly appreciated. The Union acknowledges the sacrifices and inconveniences occasioned by the strike and appeals for continued understanding and cooperation as efforts towards the restoration of normal academic activities and sustainable industrial harmony are pursued,” the statement said. ASUU Logo ASUU reaffirmed its commitment to industrial harmony, constructive dialogue and the restoration of normal academic activities, while stressing the need for the faithful implementation of the resolutions reached. It urged the Taraba State Government, the university management and all relevant parties to demonstrate good faith by ensuring the full and timely implementation of the resolutions contained in the communiqué and the Memorandum of Action (MoA). “The sustainability of industrial harmony and the uninterrupted academic calendar depend on mutual trust, accountability and strict adherence to agreed commitments. “Accordingly, all parties are urged to honour their respective obligations to prevent a recurrence of the dispute and safeguard the interests of staff, students, the University and the wider education sector,” the statement added. item.title: United Nigeria Airlines begins Jos flights to Lagos, Kano, Owerri
item.description: United Nigeria Airlines will commence scheduled flight operations from Jos to Lagos, Kano and Owerri on November 24 and 29, 2026, providing residents of Plateau State with additional air connections to other parts of the country. The airline said tickets for the new routes were already available for purchase. The Lagos–Jos–Lagos route will operate four times weekly on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays, while the Jos–Kano–Jos and Jos–Owerri–Jos routes will each operate twice weekly. Flights between Jos and Kano will operate on Tuesdays and Fridays, while those between Jos and Owerri will run on Wednesdays and Sundays. However, because the Owerri airport is currently closed, operations on the Jos–Owerri route will commence on Sunday, November 29, five days after the initial launch date. The development follows the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Plateau State Government and United Nigeria Airlines on Monday, November 9, at the office of the Commissioner for Transport, Jatau Gyang, in Jos. Under the agreement, the airline will introduce scheduled services on the Jos–Kano and Jos–Owerri routes, which the state government said were previously not served. Speaking after the signing, Gyang said the partnership was part of the state government’s broader efforts to position Plateau as a leading destination for investment, tourism, commerce and economic opportunities. He commended the airline’s management for its confidence in the state’s vision. According to him, the Jos–Owerri route will ease movement between Plateau and the South-East and South-South regions, thereby supporting trade, investment, tourism and social exchanges. He said the Jos–Kano connection would further strengthen Plateau’s relationship with the North-West, which he described as home to major commercial and industrial centres offering opportunities for business partnerships and trade. Responding on behalf of the airline, its Managing Director, Mazi Osita Okonkwo, said the agreement was significant because it would connect the South-East, South-West and North-Central regions. He described Plateau as a strategic state and assured that the airline would maintain its service standards. Okonkwo also commended Governor Caleb Mutfwang for his vision and strategic direction, while acknowledging Gyang’s efforts in facilitating the agreement. Passengers can book flights through the airline’s website, mobile application or accredited travel agents. item.title: University of America challenges NUC over illegal operations
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The National Universities Commission (NUC) and the University of America, Curaçao, have disagreed over the legality of the institution’s academic operations in Nigeria, with the commission warning prospective students against seeking admission into its programmes. The NUC had declared the institution’s operations in Nigeria illegal, alleging that it was admitting students, running academic programmes and claiming to award degrees through unauthorised campuses and learning centres across the country. However, the university has challenged the commission’s position, insisting that its legal existence as a foreign institution is distinct from the regulatory status of its learning support centres in Nigeria. In a public notice issued on Tuesday, the NUC’s Director of Public Affairs, Rita Okonjo, said the institution, also known as the University of America, had not been authorised to operate or award degrees in Nigeria. She identified the centres allegedly linked to the institution as Cosmopolitan International Business School (CIBS), Garki, Abuja; its purported Federal Capital Territory learning centre; and the University of America College of Science and Technology, also known as UAPOLY, Ekpoma, Edo State. Okonjo said the commission’s investigations showed that the institution was not accredited by any agency recognised by the United States Department of Education or the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA). She explained that its purported listing in the Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS), as well as claimed registrations in California and Florida, did not constitute accreditation or authorisation to award recognised university degrees. The NUC spokesperson also dismissed claims that the institution had obtained approval from the Federal Ministry of Education, the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board, the National Board for Technical Education and the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria. According to her, even if such approvals had been obtained, they would not confer the authority to operate a university or award degrees in Nigeria. The commission expressed concern over advertisements by the institution offering programmes in law, nursing science, engineering, pharmaceutical science, aerospace and rocket engineering, as well as postgraduate qualifications, including PhD degrees. It also raised concerns about promises of National Youth Service Corps mobilisation, professional recognition and opportunities to obtain green cards to live and work in the United States or Europe. Okonjo warned that qualifications obtained from unapproved institutions would not be recognised for NYSC mobilisation, professional registration with relevant Nigerian regulatory bodies or admission into the Nigerian Law School. item.title: Fountain of Life denies closure amid leadership crisis
item.description: By OLAYINKA LATONA LAGOS — The Fountain of Life Church has denied reports that its premises have been sealed, insisting that the church remains open, although access to its facilities is currently restricted amid an ongoing leadership dispute. The church, in a post on its official Instagram page, shared a graphic bearing the inscription, “DON’T BELIEVE THE NOISE! CHURCH IS NOT SEALED,” while inviting worshippers to attend its Sunday service. The clarification comes amid a leadership crisis involving Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and the church’s board, which has generated public attention in recent days. However, a visit by Vanguard correspondents to the church premises revealed restricted access, with activities appearing limited. There was no visible presence of police personnel at the premises, while private security operatives were stationed at the entrance. Efforts by a Vanguard reporter to gain access to the church were unsuccessful, as a security official said only persons with official business within the premises would be allowed in. The restricted access comes despite the church’s public invitation to worshippers to attend Sunday’s service. The church had earlier announced the postponement of its 2026 Thanksgiving Service, initially scheduled for Sunday, November 22, stating that a new date would be communicated. The developments come against the backdrop of a legal battle over the church’s leadership. The Lagos State High Court had restrained Odukoya from holding himself out as Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of the church following an application by the church’s Incorporated Trustees. Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin granted the interim orders on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, in a suit filed by the trustees. The court also restrained Odukoya, whether acting personally or through proxies, from interfering with, disrupting or obstructing the church’s activities, governance and other operations. The orders were granted ex parte, meaning they were made without first hearing Odukoya’s response to the application. However, the court preserved his right to apply to set aside the orders or respond to the substantive claims after being served with the court processes. The case was adjourned until December 1, 2026, for mention. The leadership dispute became public on November 17, when a faction of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that it no longer recognised Odukoya as senior pastor, citing a succession video reportedly recorded by the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, in December 2021. The trustees subsequently named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader. However, Odukoya and the church leadership rejected the decision, maintaining that his appointment as senior pastor in September 2023 was valid. item.title: Gunmen attack, machete former Super Eagles captain Odegbami
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta ABEOKUTA — Former Super Eagles captain and football administrator, Chief Segun Odegbami, has sustained injuries following an attack by three armed men at his residence in Abeokuta, Ogun State. The incident reportedly occurred at about 2:30 a.m. on Friday at his residence in the Ibara Government Reservation Area (GRA). Sources in the neighbourhood said the attackers allegedly overpowered members of his domestic staff and driver before gaining access to his bedroom, where he was attacked with machetes. Odegbami, 74, is the proprietor of Eagles 7 Sports Radio 103.7 FM and a former captain of Nigeria’s national football team. A resident, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the attackers initially asked to see the former international but were told by his domestic staff that he was not at home. The source said the attackers reportedly became suspicious after noticing that the generator was running, suggesting that someone was inside the residence. According to the resident, the assailants allegedly assaulted the domestic staff before making their way into Odegbami’s bedroom, where they attacked him. The source added that Odegbami reportedly resisted the attackers during the incident, forcing them to flee the residence. He was subsequently taken to an undisclosed hospital for medical attention. The incident was reported to the police, although the motive behind the attack had yet to be established. Meanwhile, the Ogun State Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, has visited Odegbami to sympathise with him and assure him of the command’s commitment to investigating the incident. In a statement issued by the command’s spokesperson, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, the commissioner said he had ordered an immediate and thorough investigation to identify and apprehend those responsible. Ojajuni also wished the former football international a speedy recovery and assured him that the police were treating the incident seriously. The police confirmed that Odegbami had been discharged from the hospital, adding that investigative efforts were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack and bring those responsible to justice. The commissioner urged members of the public to remain calm and provide credible information that could assist the investigation through established police communication channels.
